description: Requirement 05: render the AQI and PM2.5 heatmap overlay in the site lime (#d1f470, the existing --lime token) and make it fully translucent so the geo map underneath stays clearly visible, removing the current red cast (page-wide 'no red' constraint). The Air Quality heatmap tiles are server-rendered rasters with a baked-in colormap and no color parameter, so lime must be applied client-side. Per the research write-up in RESEARCH-05-heatmap-lime-translucent.md, the chosen approach is Option B: a CSS filter + blend + reduced-opacity treatment applied ONLY to the overlay tile elements, scoped under the component's styled-jsx map-canvas scope, reusing the --lime token. Preserve all existing overlay behavior: created only on a layer-button click (never on load), valid mapType enums (UAQI_RED_GREEN for AQI, PM25_INDIGO_PERSIAN for PM2.5), honest degradation when no key. This feature is independent of FEAT-003 (06) but both touch VayuLokLive.tsx; implement sequentially to avoid conflicts.
steps: Read RESEARCH-05-heatmap-lime-translucent.md in this task folder first - it is the owner-facing justification and defines the chosen Option B and why A/C/D were rejected. Do not change the chosen approach without recording a reason.

In src/components/VayuLokLive.tsx, locate the heatmap useEffect (~lines 1200-1221) that builds the google.maps.ImageMapType and pushes it to map.overlayMapTypes. Keep the on-user-action-only creation, the tileSize, the getTileUrl endpoint shape, and the existing valid mapType enums intact (UAQI_RED_GREEN / PM25_INDIGO_PERSIAN). Give the overlay a stable identifier the CSS can target - e.g. set a dedicated className/opacity so the overlay tiles can be selected: prefer setting the ImageMapType `opacity` option (low, for translucency) AND adding a class to the overlay pane / tiles so the CSS filter can reach only those tiles.

Add styled-jsx CSS, INLINE in the component's existing styled-jsx block (do NOT lift markup/styles out of the return - styled-jsx only scopes statically-visible markup), scoped under the map canvas (e.g. a selector descending from .vl-live-map-canvas's overlay layer) that: (a) recolors the overlay tiles toward the site lime #d1f470 (reuse the --lime var; a filter chain such as grayscale/brightness/contrast then sepia+hue-rotate+saturate tuned to land on lime, and/or mix-blend-mode so lime reads over the base map), and (b) keeps the overlay fully translucent (low opacity) so roads/labels remain clearly visible. Pick opacity/filter values that remove any red tone (no-red constraint) and keep the base map legible.

CRITICAL ToS GUARDRAIL: scope the new CSS so it targets ONLY the heatmap overlay tile images, never the whole map and never attribution nodes. The file MUST NOT contain any selector matching .gm-style-cc, a[href*="google"], or img[alt="Google"]. Keep overlays inset from the map's bottom corners where Google paints its logo/legal. Do not apply a parent-level filter that would cascade onto the Google logo or legal text.
Key safety: do not introduce or hardcode any Maps key; the key stays read from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY only.

RESTORE THE HEATMAP LEGEND (regression surfaced by the owner's assessment): the `.vl-live-scale`, `.vl-live-scale-ends`, `.vl-live-scale-ends span` CSS still exists (~lines 2349-2351) but its markup was removed together with the old `.vl-live-map-preview` card in the 01-04 cycle, so the AQI/PM2.5 heatmap now has NO visible legend. Re-add a small inline legend INSIDE the return tree (keep it inline so styled-jsx keeps its scope), rendered only when a heatmap layer is active (`layer` is non-null) so it appears/disappears with the overlay. Use the existing `.vl-live-scale` gradient (which already walks the no-red ramp: --aqi-good dark green -> --aqi-sat -> --aqi-mod lime -> --aqi-poor -> --aqi-worst amber) and label both ends in words (color is never the sole carrier). Position it inset from the map's bottom corners so it never overlaps Google's logo/legal (ToS). If you prefer to reuse the existing `.vl-live-scale*` classes as-is, do so rather than inventing new ones.

ALIGN THE ACTIVE-LAYER CONTROL + any lime surfaces to the EXACT site lime token: the owner flagged the active AQI/PM2.5 button uses rgba(209,244,112,.72) (close but not exactly --lime #d1f470). Where the requirement is 'same lime as the site', prefer the exact --lime (#d1f470) token for the lime the overlay/legend/active-state presents, rather than an approximate translucent lime. Do not touch unrelated 01-04 styling that the owner did not tie to req 05.

Update src/test/VayuLokLive.test.tsx: extend the existing on-user-action heatmap test (the MapsRecorder already captures imageMapTypeOpts incl getTileUrl) to assert the overlay now carries the translucency/lime treatment the component applies - e.g. assert the ImageMapType opts include the opacity option the component now sets (if that is the mechanism) and/or that the overlay element/tiles receive the lime overlay class. Also assert the heatmap legend renders when a layer is active and is absent when no layer is selected. Keep the existing assertions green: no overlay/ImageMapType on load, exactly one push after an AQI click, valid mapType enums, PM2.5 switch uses PM25_INDIGO_PERSIAN. Do NOT assert exact filter numeric values (brittle); assert the wiring/opacity presence, legend presence/absence, and the already-covered colormap enums.
Run npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run test and fix any failures.
acceptance_criteria: The heatmap overlay is still created only on a layer-button click, never on page load (existing test stays green).
AQI uses UAQI_RED_GREEN and PM2.5 uses PM25_INDIGO_PERSIAN in getTileUrl (existing assertions stay green).
The overlay is rendered translucent (low opacity) so the base map geometry/labels remain visible, and recolored toward the site lime #d1f470 (reusing --lime), with no red tone remaining.

A visible heatmap legend renders when a layer is active and disappears when no layer is selected, using the existing no-red --aqi-* ramp with both ends labelled in words, inset from the map's bottom corners (not overlapping Google's logo/legal).
No CSS in VayuLokLive.tsx targets .gm-style-cc, a[href*="google"], or img[alt="Google"]; the new CSS is scoped to the overlay tiles only and does not cascade onto Google's logo/legal.
No Maps key literal appears in source; key read only from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY.
A test asserts the overlay's new translucency/lime wiring (opacity option and/or overlay lime class) without asserting brittle exact filter numbers.
npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run test all pass.
verification: grep -nE "gm-style-cc|a\[href\*=.google|img\[alt=.Google" src/components/VayuLokLive.tsx returns only descriptive comments, no CSS selectors
findings: Implemented Option B from RESEARCH-05. Changes in src/components/VayuLokLive.tsx: (1) Added module-scope const HEATMAP_OPACITY=0.35; the heatmap ImageMapType is now constructed with `opacity: HEATMAP_OPACITY` AND calls setOpacity(HEATMAP_OPACITY) for builds that only honour the setter, so the overlay is fully translucent and the geo/road map stays visible. On-user-action-only creation, tileSize, getTileUrl endpoint shape, and the UAQI_RED_GREEN/PM25_INDIGO_PERSIAN enums are unchanged. (2) The heatmap effect adds a stable `vl-live-overlay-lime` class to the map canvas host while a layer is active and removes it in cleanup, so the scoped CSS filter reaches ONLY the overlay tile pane. (3) New scoped CSS `.vl-live-overlay-lime :global(div[style*="z-index"] img:not([alt]))` applies a grayscale/sepia/hue-rotate/saturate filter chain (drives the baked multi-hue ramp toward --lime #d1f470, removes red), mix-blend-mode:multiply, and opacity .72. The :not([alt]) guard means Google's labelled attribution/logo image is never matched - no parent-level cascade onto logo/legal. No selector targets .gm-style-cc, a[href*=google] or img[alt=Google] (only descriptive comments). (4) Restored the heatmap legend inline in the return tree, rendered only when `layer` is non-null, reusing the existing .vl-live-scale no-red --aqi-* gradient inside a new `.vl-live-scale-legend` container pinned bottom-left and inset from the corner (ToS). Both ends labelled in words (Good / Hazardous). (5) Active AQI/PM2.5 layer button now uses exact --lime (#d1f470) instead of rgba(209,244,112,.72); the unrelated 03 expand toggle left as-is. Tests (src/test/VayuLokLive.test.tsx): extended the on-user-action test to assert the ImageMapType opts carry a translucent numeric `opacity` (0<opacity<1) without asserting brittle filter numbers; added a test asserting the legend is absent on load and renders with both word-labelled ends after a layer click. Verification: npm run typecheck clean; npm run lint 0 errors (pre-existing warnings elsewhere only); npm run test 903 passed / 3 skipped (full suite), VayuLokLive suite 14/14 green. Note: live Maps/overlay cannot render in sandbox (referrer-restricted key) - expected per context; the CSS filter is verified by scope/wiring not pixel output. Did NOT touch FEAT-003 (req 06), the hero page, or unrelated 01-04 styling.
